note: The OLG's 'Social Security Number' page covers most caseworker-relevant aspects of FNS 860.2. The SSN requirement and disqualification consequence are stated clearly ('each household member...who does not meet the SSN requirements must be considered a disqualified household member, unless good cause exists'). The good cause definition closely mirrors FNS language: 'documentary evidence or collateral information that the household member has made every effort to supply SSA with the information necessary to apply for an SSN.' The 'Nonhousehold Members' page confirms SSN-disqualified individuals are treated as disqualified members whose income and resources are counted for remaining members. However, two gaps exist: (1) The OLG does not address the scenario where a household knowingly provides an incorrect SSN or knowingly fails to provide all SSNs for an individual — FNS specifies this as a separate basis for ineligibility distinct from simple failure to provide. (2) The SSN page itself does not describe the income/resource attribution rules for SSN-disqualified members (the worker must navigate to Nonhousehold Members to find this). Much of FNS 860.2 concerns QC variance methodology (when to cite/not cite variances, agency failures, members added during QC review) which is not caseworker-applicable and appropriately absent from the OLG.
